chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from al-Ahwal, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about fasting two Thursdays with a Wednesday in between them.
He replied: As for Thursday, it is a day in which deeds are presented; and as for Wednesday, it is a day in which Hell was created; and as for the fast, it is a shield.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of fasting on the two Thursdays and the Wednesday in between?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the specific virtues of fasting on the two Thursdays and the intervening Wednesday of the lunar month. The Prophet (peace be upon him) identifies Thursday as the day deeds are presented to God and Wednesday as the day Hell was created, with fasting serving as a shield (junnah) against its fire. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on voluntary fasting as a means of spiritual protection and divine acceptance.
